absent: Exact numeric values for private and shared counts, frame sizes, identifier widths, priority widths and file modes.
Complete field layouts and sizes for distributor, interrupt descriptor, per CPU and virtual emulation structures.
Ordering relative to device creation, address assignment, input output registration and interrupt tree setup outside these fragments.
Teardown, error propagation and partial failure cleanup for routing, debug and direct injection paths.
Concurrency guarantees for pause, sleep, request flags and nested context switching beyond observed locks and flags.
Resolution tables, mask definitions and translation rules for system register storage locations.
Conditions selecting virtual model types and host capability detection for direct injection generations.

findings.text: Top level distributor bring-up is idempotent and orders model specific setup before per CPU reset, default routing, debug exposure and completion marking, refusing to proceed while virtual CPU creation is still settling.
Debug support exposes virtual interrupt controller state through a read only file owned by the virtual machine debug directory.

Legacy shared interrupt storage is allocated once, with each descriptor receiving an identifier beyond the private range, an empty queue, an initialized lock, a cleared owner, a default target and a zeroed reference count, plus model dependent defaults for addressing and grouping. Unknown models fail and release storage.
Per CPU reset dispatches on the configured virtual model and host capability, selecting among the newest path, the older compatible path and the intermediate path.
The oldest CPU interface reset clears its virtual control state so that binary point fields return to architectural defaults.

The intermediate CPU interface reset clears its virtual control state, and for guests using that model it forces system register enablement with bypass disabled plus a defined pending base, while deriving identifier and priority widths from host interface capabilities.
The newest CPU interface reset presents fixed identifier and priority widths to the guest independent of wider host support.
Default interrupt routing establishes an identity mapping from each shared index to the same pin on the single virtual chip.

Direct injection setup is a no-op without host support or when already done, otherwise it allocates per CPU virtual emulation structures, binds host doorbells with enablement policy that differs on newer hardware, and releases everything if any step fails.
Newest model initialization rejects nested configurations and restricts userspace driven private interrupts to the single architected software signal intersected with implemented capabilities.
Oldest CPU interface device setup binds a fixed register region table with shared input output operations and reports a fixed frame size.
Oldest address validation rejects wrapping distributor or CPU ranges and requires the two frames to be strictly non-overlapping.

Intermediate resource mapping requires defined redistributor and distributor addresses, non-overlapping frames, prior initialization, and then optionally enables direct software generated interrupts on capable hosts.
Direct software generated interrupt reconfiguration pauses the whole guest, toggles per CPU direct mode according to whether any requests exist, then resumes the guest.
Guest halt marks every virtual CPU as paused and requests sleep, while resume clears the mark and wakes each CPU.

Enabling direct software interrupts marks each per CPU signal as hardware backed, binds its host mapping, transfers configuration and pending latch to the virtual emulation structure, and activates the host path. Disabling reverses the transfer by sampling host pending state back into the latch and deactivating.
Configuration synchronization copies enablement, grouping and priority from the emulated descriptor into the virtual emulation slot indexed by interrupt identity.

Newest resource mapping only requires prior initialization. Finalization builds exposure and trigger mode masks from the first virtual CPU by including owned signals plus the architected software signal, and is idempotent once that signal is already advertised.
Architecture interrupt controller readiness query delegates directly to virtual distributor completion state.

Wait for interrupt handling synchronizes virtual CPU interface state around a halted window bracketed by flag updates without preemption. Sleep waits until neither stopped nor paused and re-arms itself when awakened early. Suspend repeats until userspace makes the CPU runnable, reporting wakeup through a system event exit when runnable.

Virtual CPU request processing aborts the virtual machine dead case, then handles sleep, reset, pending interrupt clearing, asynchronous distributor updates, stolen time accounting, direct injection reload without preemption, performance monitor reload and restore, suspend with possible early exit, dirty ring signalling and finally nested work.

Nested request handling unmaps stage two ranges under write exclusion when flagged, maps virtualized system control state when flagged, and injects pending guest hypervisor interrupts last because that step may switch execution context.
Nested interrupt injection is suppressed when executing at the higher privilege without trapping and without interrupt masking, otherwise it delivers a virtual interrupt exception at that privilege.

Nested exception delivery rejects non-nesting configurations, uses a fast path when already in the higher privilege context or in compatible user context with virtualization controls set, otherwise it commits program counter state around a put plus inject plus load sequence guarded against preemption and followed by performance monitor transition.

Higher privilege exception injection records tracing information and maps synchronous, interrupt and error types to distinct pending states, storing the syndrome value for synchronous and error cases and warning on unknown types.

System register write resolves the storage location, applies special handling for select registers, sanitizes whitelisted values, follows mapping and translation indirections when present, updates the physical backing when loaded, and always updates the in-memory copy.

Distributor bring-up and direct injection setup plus reconfiguration require the virtual machine configuration lock held. Private interrupt finalization takes that lock exclusively. Per interrupt toggling uses interrupt level exclusion with interrupts saved. Nested unmap uses write exclusion on the memory lock. Virtual interface synchronization and nested context switches disable preemption.

Observed distributor state comprises model selection, shared count and array, completion flag, base addresses, direct injection virtual machine with per CPU pointers and counts, and newest private masks for userspace, exposure and trigger mode. Interrupt descriptors carry identity, queue linkage, lock, ownership, targeting, reference count, hardware backing, pending and config fields. Per CPU state carries interface controls, pending base, width counts and emulation structures.

Private range size defines the base offset for shared identifiers, legacy total defines the default shared count, software signal count bounds direct injection loops, and one architected software private identity selects the userspace drivable signal.

Virtual model selectors distinguish oldest, intermediate and newest distributor types, host capability flags distinguish direct injection generations, and fixed frame sizes bound distributor and CPU interface mappings.

Hazards include concurrent virtual CPU creation during bring-up, use before initialization for mapping and injection paths, overlapping or undefined base addresses, allocation failures for shared storage routing tables and emulation structures, doorbell request failures requiring teardown, and unsupported nesting on the newest model.
